objective.metric: equal-cell mean full-canvas per-pixel OKLab ΔE, the fitting objective of §5.130 §1, with the declared union 6-CSS-px-eroded body ΔE, body linear Rec.709 Y mean and body population SD published beside it per cell
objective.tier: WebGPU, and only WebGPU (contract X1). The CSS tier's derivation is captured beside the result for the record and gates nothing.
objective.selection: on the calibration cells of a term and on nothing else. Controls are read before and after and may refuse a form; they are not minimised over. Holdout is read once, at the end, on the frozen result, and no constant moves after it.

terms.name: the dark thin response over a bright backdrop
terms.reading: claims §5.139 §6: `light-solid__capsule-button__inactive` in dark reads web 0.15637 / native 0.93261, body ΔE 0.43838, and `light-solid__rrect-sm__inactive` 0.16225 / 0.93261, body ΔE 0.43179 — the two largest readings on the bed. At thick span the same backdrop reads 0.09339 / 0.11753, so it is the thin row alone. §5.130's table recorded the dark `backdropToneResponseThin` far ordinate as an extrapolation of a selected family, not a measured bright-background level.
terms.constantInScope: packages/platform-web/src/receded-profile.ts, the DARK entry's `backdropToneResponseThin[2]` — the ordinate at `backdropToneAnchorX[2]` = 0.9505, which is `light-solid`'s own encoded-space mean. Nothing else in that entry, and nothing in the light entry.

calibration.why: span 32 is `sizeSpanMin`, where `sizeThickness` is exactly 0 and the response's thin row is evaluated with no admixture of the thick row at all. It is therefore the one span on the bed at which the thin far ordinate is identified alone. Both scales, because §5.128 §5 binds every estimate to the scale it was measured at and the ordinate is not scale-indexed. Group A, supplying — the fit spends no checking cell for this term.

cells: the recovered dark thin cells over `checkerboard` and `photo` in §5.130's own bed, read NATIVE-ONLY out of the committed fixtures
controls.why: the far ordinate is not a local constant. `backdropToneResponseLevel` interpolates monotonically (Fritsch–Carlson) through three knots, so moving the third moves the derivative at the second and reshapes the whole curve above `backdropToneAnchorX[1]`. Every dark thin cell over a backdrop whose encoded mean lies between 0.2706 and 0.9505 moves with it. The two solid anchors' own thin cells hold the curve's lower end; the structured dark thin cells are where a raised far ordinate would be paid for, and they are §5.130 calibration ids, so reading them costs nothing and they can bound nothing. They are a REFUSAL instrument, not a fitting input: if the one-parameter family cannot hold the calibration cell and the controls together, the form is refused and reported, not compromised into a joint minimum.
controls.spend: none. The recovered-fixture readings are native-only where they are outside this bed, and the bed's own control cells are supplying (group A).

holdout.why: span 44 on the same backdrop, one rung up the thickness ramp: `sizeThickness(44)` is 0.0923, so the response mixes 2.4% of the thick row in. It is the cell that says whether one ordinate fitted where the thin row stands alone predicts a cell where it does not. Group E, and in the DARK scheme it has no recovered fixture at all (§5.139 §4), so no fit has ever selected on it.
holdout.whatItIsAndIsNot: its NATIVE ordinate is already published (§5.139 §6, 0.93261), so this holdout is not a check against an unseen reference. It is a check of the fitted FORM's prediction on a cell the fit did not select on. The cells whose vitrea-against-native distance has never been read at all are the bound's own checking set, which this term's fit does not touch.
holdout.readOnce: after the configuration is frozen, once, with no constant permitted to move in response.

notTouchedAndScoredByTheBound: apple-macos-26.5-{1x,2x}-dark-standard/hc-text__rrect-sm__inactive — span 32, a structured bright backdrop, group D
apple-macos-26.5-{1x,2x}-dark-standard/light-solid__rrect-ml__inactive — span 128, above `sizeSpanMax`, so the thin row does not reach it at all

terms.name: the accessibility recede's occlusion
terms.reading: claims §5.139 §6: over `dark-solid` under Increase Contrast the reference is an opaque near-white panel at every span — 0.99445 at span 48, 0.9937 at 80, 0.9935 at 96 — while vitrea follows the backdrop down at the thin end, 0.58408 at span 48 recovering to 0.9560 by span 80, and 0.53328 under Reduce Transparency. §5.130 fitted `increasedOcclusionLift` on 1x light accessibility bodies and recorded that their different native levels are not fully expressible by this shared policy fold; the fold misses by 0.41 Y, in the direction that defeats the setting.
terms.constantsInScope: packages/platform-web/src/receded-profile.ts, the LIGHT entry's accessibility fold — `increasedOcclusionLift`, and whichever other EXISTING profile-document field the cells show the occlusion regime actually needs. No field is added to `MaterialProfile`: a fit moves the profile documents and nothing else. The dark entry carries no accessibility field (§5.130 §6) and gains none here.
whyThisTermCostsACheckingCell: The two accessibility profiles declare 14 of the bed's ids and 12 of them are group D — the checking set. The bed has no supplying cell under either accessibility policy: groups A, B and C are declared on the four standard profiles only, and group E's two accessibility ids are §5.130 calibration ids over structured backdrops.

So there is no partition of this term that leaves the bound's scoring population untouched. The choice is between fitting the term on one scored cell per policy and refusing to fit it at all, and W27 Decision Log 17 rules that it is fitted.

The cost is therefore declared here, before the fit, rather than discovered in the verdict: after this fit the bound's clauses 2 and 3 on `apple-macos-26.5-1x-light-increased-contrast` and `apple-macos-26.5-1x-light-reduced-transparency` are NO LONGER an unspent check on `dark-solid__rrect-48__inactive`. The bound is still applied exactly as §5.134 §6 declares it — not narrowed, not re-scoped, not re-declared — and the verdict names the spend beside the profile it touches. The other eleven checking cells in each accessibility profile stay unspent, and the four standard profiles' checking sets are untouched by this term.

calibration.why: span 48 is the thin end where the fold misses by 0.41 Y, and `dark-solid` is the uniform backdrop that makes the miss a level reading rather than a structure reading. One cell per policy because macOS force-couples Increase Contrast with Reduce Transparency: both profiles resolve `occlusion: increased` from the SAME flag, and they differ only in `ambientTint`, which enters the same product. Two cells is the smallest set that identifies whether the two policies need one number or two.

controls.why: these four are §5.130's own '1x light accessibility body controls' — the cells the 0.92 was fitted on, calibration ids that can bound nothing, so reading them adds no spend. They are the term's refusal instrument: they decide whether the reference's accessibility panel is backdrop-INDEPENDENT. A form that takes the recede to opacity is right only if the reference reads the same level over a structured backdrop as over `dark-solid`; if it does not, the cells refuse an occlusion floor and the term is reported rather than fitted.

holdout.why: the same backdrop one rung up the span ladder, where the reference reads 0.9937 and vitrea already reaches 0.9560 without any change. If the term's form is right the residual there is small and span-independent; if the form has merely bought the thin end at the thick end's expense, this is the cell that says so. It is a group D checking cell and its vitrea-against-native distance is published in §5.139's matrix, so — like T1's holdout — it checks the fitted form's prediction, not an unseen reference.
holdout.readOnce: after the configuration is frozen, once, with no constant permitted to move in response.

notTouchedAndScoredByTheBound: the remaining ten group D ids in each accessibility profile — the four `hc-text` cells, the three `checkerboard*` cells, `light-solid__rrect-ml__inactive`, `dark-solid__rrect-md-clear20__inactive` and `checkerboard__rrect-ml__inactive`
